To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the central bank's endogenously determined interest rate trajectory is a good predictor of future policy rates and the market's failure to forecast future policy rates does not always mean that there is no monetary policy inertia.

(i) the central bank's endogenously smoothed interest rate trajectory contains a large amount of information about future interest rates, (ii) the market does not use this information in its expectations about future rates, and (iii) the market is not able to forecast the large amount of future interest rate variability that is contained in the central bank's smoothed interest rate trajectory.

the central bank's endogenously determined interest rate trajectory has a small but significant forecastable component and the market's failure to forecast this component of future rates does not necessarily imply limited central bank policy inertia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the issue of monetary policy inertia and the degree to which the market anticipates future policy rates.
how to measure the monetary policy inertia in the presence of endogenous interest rate trajectories.
how to improve the forecasting performance of the interest rate path.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
central bank's policy rate inertia is a complex and multifaceted issue that cannot be explained by one or two variables alone.
the market's failure to forecast large portion of variability does not always mean that central banks have limited policy inertia.

the market's failure to forecast large portion of future interest rates does not necessarily imply limited policy inertia, and that the market's success to predict future rates does not necessarily mean high policy inertia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
central banks are not always as inert as we thought.
the central bank's endogenously generated interest rate trajectory is a good indicator for the central bank's policy stance.
the market's failure to forecast large portion of future rates' variability does not necessarily mean that the central bank has limited policy inertia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
central banks' interest rate trajectories are not only highly predictable but also contain a lot of useful information about future interest rate movements.
the central bank's endogenously determined interest rate trajectory can be an important source of forecastable future rates.
, when it comes to the monetary policy, the future is not necessarily predictable.
